subject.title: feat(slack): Support Slack RTS (Real-Time Search) API via assistant action tokens

question: Should OpenClaw add Slack RTS as a separate assistant action-token search path, and what token containment, read-target policy, and scope rules should it enforce?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the feature would handle event-scoped Slack credentials and workspace-wide search results, so automation should not choose the product/security boundary without maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve narrow RTS contract
options.body: Implement `assistant.search.context` in the Slack plugin with event-scoped token containment, read-target/privacy enforcement, docs, tests, and redacted live Slack proof.

options.title: Consolidate Slack search first
options.body: Define one Slack search contract that covers RTS and any user-token search before accepting implementation work.

options.title: Defer workspace search
options.body: Keep this issue open but block implementation until maintainers are ready to own the token and privacy model.

recommendation.title: Approve narrow RTS contract
recommendation.body: Implement `assistant.search.context` in the Slack plugin with event-scoped token containment, read-target/privacy enforcement, docs, tests, and redacted live Slack proof.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle has the strongest recent Slack assistant/action history and already routed broad Slack search work back to this issue.
